evidence.paraphrase: The narrator reports an explanation attributing the bell sound to a large owl.
evidence.quote: he said that the sound proceeded from a very large owl, in a hollow tree; a sort of learned owl, that continually knocked its head against the branches.

evidence.paraphrase: People attempted to investigate the source of the bell sound.
evidence.quote: Many persons now went to the wood, for the sake of getting the place, but one only returned with a sort of explanation; for nobody went far enough...

evidence.paraphrase: The character intends to travel far beyond usual limits to locate the bell.
evidence.quote: I must and will find the bell, even if I am obliged to go to the end of the world.

evidence.paraphrase: The king promises a reward for discovering the source of the bell sound.
evidence.quote: The king of the country was also observant of it, and vowed that he who could discover whence the sounds proceeded, should have the title of ‘Universal Bell-ringer,’ even if it were not really a bell.

evidence.paraphrase: The characters realize the bell is imaginary.
evidence.quote: Now we are there! In reality the bell does not exist; it is only a fancy that people have taken into their heads!
